about: One record per detector and per repository-level check: the corpus it was measured on, the date, the counts before and after each calibration, the named exclusions, and where the prose account lives. `reproduce` says whether the number can be recomputed by somebody else: a command, the tool version that ran it, and a corpus manifest pinning each repository to a commit. Records written before 1.6.0 carry a null reproduce block with the reason, because a measurement whose corpus was never pinned cannot be pinned afterwards without inventing the commits.

records.name: doc_test_count_drift
records.corpus: 2026-09-10: HERALD (135 claimed, 321 collected), the case this detector was built from, plus a ghost_tools self-scan where 3 of 3 findings were false and produced the claim-shape filters. 2026-09-12: the whole 38-repository library, at the commits in the manifest below.
records.before: 65 findings raised across the library, after every claim-shape filter including the named-owner rule added in 1.7.0
records.after: 0 of the 65 is a stale claim about the scanned repository's own current suite. Read individually: 24 name another project in a comparison table, 13 are scoped to a single test file or a single pytest command, 12 sit in a dated record or status report, and the remaining 16 are hedged, scoped or historical on reading ('Roughly 670 tests' in an investor deck, 'the repository's July 2026 governance status recorded 270 tests', '161/161 tests' as a phase pass ratio). Measured precision on this corpus: 0.
exclusions: one-directional: only a documented count the real count has grown well past (min_growth_ratio and min_absolute_growth both required)
claims filtered as delta, transition, quotation, attribution or attributed-to-a-named-owner never become findings and are not in the 65
disclosed: the static test_* count is a lower bound; parametrize only pushes the true count higher
the classification of the 65 is a reading, not a mechanical rule. The counts per category are reproducible from the snippets the findings already carry; the category boundaries are a judgement

precision 0 is a measurement of THIS corpus, one person's library of design documents, status reports and investor material. A corpus of ordinary READMEs would likely score differently, and the one recorded true positive (HERALD) came from exactly such a case
the finding count was not the defect count. This detector's pool was recommended as the highest-value remedy target on the strength of 65 plus 64 findings, before anybody read them

reproduce.command: python -m ghost_buster.cli <repo> --tests --json, once per repository, then filter findings to detector doc_test_count_drift and read each evidence.snippet

records.name: unreachable_declared_state
records.corpus: SWIZZLE 70db473 (105 files, 67 enum members across 13 enums) and ghost_tools 1320339 (4 enums)
exclusions: enums where NO member is ever produced (reconstructed from data: an HTTP status, a wire protocol). Without this the detector's entire output would be such enums
classes that do not inherit an Enum base, so a settings class of upper-case constants is not treated as a state machine
lower-case class attributes, which are not enum members by convention
members named only inside a module-level upper-case constant holding a COLLECTION -- a lookup table is a comparison in disguise. A constant holding a single member is still a production. Added 1.7.6
disclosed: a member is matched by NAME, not by resolving the enum, so a member name shared by two enums is treated as produced for both. An AST-only tool; the cost is a lost finding rather than an invented one
it does not claim the state is unreachable. Enum(value) reconstructs any member from data, so a stored record can still carry it -- which is worse, not better, and the finding says so

reproduce.note: Found 1 on each. On SWIZZLE: Phase.BETWEEN_RUNS, declared among four phases of which the world builder carries out three, so a case declaring it built a world without its mutation and was still judged as temporal. On ghost_tools itself: Status.REJECTED ('a human looked and said no'), which nothing produces and whose triage module does not exist. Both confirmed by hand. 1.7.6: counting lookup-table membership as production had made this detector miss a state of exactly the shape it was built to find -- it reported Status.REJECTED and stayed quiet about Status.CONFIRMED_BY_REVIEW, which is never assigned either. Findings on ghost_tools went 1 -> 5, and all five were confirmed by hand: two Status members superseded by `disposition`, and three EvidenceKind members in blackhole_extrapolator that appear only as keys in a confidence-weight table, so the table assigns confidence to evidence nothing can produce.
